knowledge_gaps: Baseline versus A cannot isolate the benefits of retrieval, recency decay, or evidence-mass shrinkage. Prespecify affordable controls before attributing gains to these mechanisms.

Evidence mass can increase through repeated items, embedding alignment, and history length without stronger preference evidence. Include repeat-count, popularity, history-length, and similarity strata; use controlled perturbations before claiming reduced isolated-action influence.

B lacks an explicit gBCE equation, calibration-factor calculation, loss reduction, and negative-sampling replacement policy. Its history-positive exclusions may also differ from baseline, adding another experimental confound.

The small initial amplitude may make A effectively inactive. Log amplitude gradients and actual candidate-score corrections, and restore identical backbone initializations rather than relying only on seed reuse.

The proposed allocation consumes the entire 43,200-second budget. Clarify remaining budget after historical trials and enforce a shared ledger, synchronized timing boundaries, and interruption-safe checkpoints.

Originality 4 and potential 7 need stronger support from closely related retrieval and history-similarity models. Difficulty 4 is plausible for the mathematical branch, but full integration, quadratic-memory overhead, and export verification remain unmeasured.

Reproducibility still requires explicit diagnostic sampling, valid-position masks, simulator-user selection, and inference broadcasting rules. Report validation gains as exploratory after historical selection; paired uncertainty is possible only if the unchanged host exposes per-user hits.
